content.user_title: Convert Taiwan Lunar Dates and Estimate Solar Terms
content.value_statement: Lunar dates, leap months, and solar terms can be difficult to determine from Gregorian dates. This skill provides local Python calculations for lunar conversion, zodiac animals, and Taiwan solar-term estimates.
actual_capabilities: Convert Gregorian dates from 1900-01-31 through 2100-12-31 to lunar year, month, day, and leap-month status.
Identify zodiac animals from the converted lunar year rather than the Gregorian year.
Estimate crossing times for all 24 solar terms using apparent solar longitude and binary search.
Report solar-term dates and times in Taiwan time, UTC+8.
Perform calculations with Python 3 standard libraries without network requests, API keys, or package installation.
limitations: Lunar conversion is limited to the included 1900-2100 table and rejects dates before 1900-01-31 or after 2100.
Solar-term times are approximate, with stated errors around 15 minutes; crossings near midnight can yield a different date.
The skill supplies code in SKILL.md, not an installed executable, and requires a Python 3 execution environment.
It does not provide a dedicated lunar-to-Gregorian conversion function or an official public-holiday schedule.

use_cases.title: Check Family Calendar Dates
use_cases.description: Convert birthdays or selected dates to lunar dates and identify leap months and zodiac animals.

use_cases.title: Prepare Seasonal Teaching Material
use_cases.description: List solar-term dates in Taiwan time and distinguish approximate crossing times from official calendar values.

use_cases.title: Prototype Offline Calendar Features
use_cases.description: Use the supplied Python functions to test lunar conversion and solar-term calculations without external services.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Date
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert 2026-09-25 to its Taiwan lunar date. Include the lunar year, month, day, leap-month status, and zodiac animal.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Year Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the lunar dates and zodiac animals for 2026-02-16 and 2026-02-17. Explain which lunar year each date belongs to.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Solar Terms
prompt_templates.prompt: Calculate Qingming, Autumn Equinox, and Winter Solstice for 2026 in UTC+8. Label times as estimates and note the stated uncertainty.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Local Calendar Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supplied Python functions to summarize lunar dates for [Gregorian dates] and all solar terms for [year]. Run in a private temporary directory. Flag unsupported dates and crossings within 15 minutes of midnight. Do not invent official verification.

output_examples.input: What is the lunar date for 2026-09-25?
output: Lunar date: year 2026, month 8, day 15; not a leap month.
Zodiac animal: Horse. This date is Mid-Autumn Festival.

output_examples.input: Which lunar year and zodiac apply to 2026-02-16 and 2026-02-17?
output: 2026-02-16: lunar year 2025, month 12, day 29; Snake year.
2026-02-17: lunar year 2026, month 1, day 1; Horse year.
The zodiac changes at Lunar New Year, not January 1.

output_examples.input: When is Qingming in 2026, according to this calculation?
output: Estimated Qingming crossing: 2026-04-05 at 02:28, Taiwan time, UTC+8.
The skill documents an official comparison time of 02:40, a 12-minute difference.
Check the official calendar for ceremonial or formal use.

best_practices: Specify Gregorian dates explicitly and use Taiwan time when requesting the current lunar date.
Preserve leap-month labels and derive zodiac animals from the converted lunar year.
Run scripts in a private directory and verify solar-term estimates against official tables when precise dates matter.
anti_patterns: Do not append to or execute a predictable shared temporary script without protecting its ownership and contents.
Do not present approximate solar-term times as exact astronomical measurements or guaranteed official dates.
Do not infer zodiac animals from January 1 or force lunar conversion outside the supported date range.

faq.question: Does this skill require internet access or an API key?
faq.answer: No. Its supplied calculations use Python 3 standard libraries and an embedded lunar table without network requests.

faq.question: Which dates support lunar conversion?
faq.answer: The conversion function supports Gregorian dates from 1900-01-31 through 2100-12-31.

faq.question: Does it identify leap months?
faq.answer: Yes. The conversion returns a leap-month flag, which should be included when reporting the lunar date.

faq.question: How accurate are the solar-term times?
faq.answer: The skill states approximately 15-minute uncertainty. Near-midnight crossings can change the reported date, so verify precise requirements against official tables.

faq.question: When does the zodiac animal change?
faq.answer: This implementation uses the lunar year. Convert the Gregorian date first, then calculate the zodiac from that lunar year.

faq.question: What is needed to run the calculations?
faq.answer: Use a Python 3 environment and the code blocks in SKILL.md. Store the complete script in a private directory before execution.
